10-k.txt:547: ITEM 1.
10-k.txt:548: BUSINESS
10-k.txt:549: GENERAL
10-k.txt:550: Where
10-k.txt:551: Food Comes From, Inc. and its subsidiaries (“WFCF,” the “Company,” “our,” “we,” or “us”)
10-k.txt:552: is a leading trusted resource for third-party verification of food production practices in North America. The Company estimates that
10-k.txt:553: it supports more than approximately 17,500 farmers, ranchers, vineyards, wineries, processors, retailers, distributors, trade associations,
10-k.txt:554: consumer brands, chefs and restaurants with a wide variety of value-added services provided through its family of verifiers. In order
10-k.txt:555: to have credibility, product claims such as gluten-free, non-GMO, non-hormone treated, humane handling, and others require verification
10-k.txt:556: by an independent third-party such as WFCF. The Company’s principal business is conducting both on-site and desk audits to verify
10-k.txt:557: that claims being made about livestock, aquaculture, crops and other food products are accurate.
10-k.txt:558: We
10-k.txt:559: also provide a wide range of professional consulting services that generate incremental revenue specific to the food and agricultural
10-k.txt:560: industry and drive sustainable value creation. Finally, the Company’s Where Food Comes From Source Verified® retail and restaurant
10-k.txt:561: labeling program utilizes the verification of product attributes to connect consumers directly to the source of the food they purchase
10-k.txt:562: through product labeling and web-based information sharing and education.
10-k.txt:563: WFCF
10-k.txt:564: was founded in 1996 and incorporated in the state of Colorado as a subchapter C corporation in 2006. The Company’s shares of common
10-k.txt:565: stock trade on the NASDAQ Capital Market (“NASDAQ”), under the stock ticker symbol, “WFCF.”
10-k.txt:566: The
10-k.txt:567: Company’s original name – Integrated Management Information, Inc. (d.b.a. IMI Global) – was changed to Where Food Comes
10-k.txt:568: From, Inc. in 2012 to better reflect the Company’s mission. Early growth was attributable to source and age verification services
10-k.txt:569: for beef producers that wanted access to markets overseas following the discovery of “mad cow” disease in the U.S. Over the
10-k.txt:570: years, WFCF has expanded its portfolio to include verification and professional services for most food groups and over 50 programs and
10-k.txt:571: organizations. This growth has been achieved both organically and through the acquisition of other companies.
10-k.txt:572: BUSINESS
10-k.txt:573: OVERVIEW
10-k.txt:574: What
10-k.txt:575: We Do
10-k.txt:576: The
10-k.txt:577: Company is one of the nation’s largest independent, third-party traceability and verification providers. We use rigorous verification
10-k.txt:578: processes on food production processes to ensure that claims made by food producers and processors are accurate. We care about food and
10-k.txt:579: other agricultural products, how it is grown and raised, the quality of what we eat, what farmers and ranchers do, and authentically
10-k.txt:580: telling that story to the consumer. Our team visits farms and ranches and looks at their plants, animals, and records, and compares the
10-k.txt:581: information we collect to specific standards or claims that farms and ranches want to make about how they are producing food. Our customers
10-k.txt:582: include top-tier players in the food and wine space.
10-k.txt:583: The
10-k.txt:584: Company also provides a wide range of professional consulting services and technology solutions that generate incremental revenue specific
10-k.txt:585: to the food and agricultural industry and drive sustainable value creation.
10-k.txt:586: 3
10-k.txt:587: The
10-k.txt:588: Company’s business benefits from growing demand by consumers, retailers and government for increased transparency into food production
10-k.txt:589: practices.
10-k.txt:590: Consumers:
10-k.txt:591: Due to concerns about social responsibility and sustainability, food safety, and an overall increase in health consciousness, consumers
10-k.txt:592: are demanding more information about the food they purchase. Third-party verification means highly trained verification specialists reviewed
10-k.txt:593: documentation and have sent independent auditors onsite to where the food came from to confirm if a claim is true.
10-k.txt:594: Retailers:
10-k.txt:595: Responding to consumer demands for increased transparency as well as to the negative impact food scandals have on their bottom lines,
10-k.txt:596: retailers are requiring their suppliers to adhere to more stringent traceability and verification of product claims. Verification and
10-k.txt:597: certification provide retailers and food service a way to differentiate themselves from their competitors. Ultimately, verification helps
10-k.txt:598: build trust while communicating how much a retailer cares about the authenticity of the claims on their products.
10-k.txt:599: Government
10-k.txt:600: Regulation:
10-k.txt:601: Regulations including the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (“USDA”) Animal Disease Traceability program,
10-k.txt:602: international export requirements, non-GMO and gluten-free testing requirements, and ingredient labeling regulations are all impacting
10-k.txt:603: product verification. Verification programs add value to products. In addition to adding value, they also enable access to new market
10-k.txt:604: opportunities, which include international exports.
10-k.txt:605: Growth
10-k.txt:606: Strategy
10-k.txt:607: Due
10-k.txt:608: to organic growth in our portfolio of auditing standards, consumer demand and acquisitions, our sales have grown rapidly from $1.1 million
10-k.txt:609: in 2006 to $24.9 million in 2025, a 19-year compounded annual growth rate (“CAGR”) of approximately 17.87%.
10-k.txt:610: Our
10-k.txt:611: growth strategy is as follows:
10-k.txt:612: ● | To cover more food groups than any other verification provider. Currently we verify to hundreds of claims, programs and markets focusing on beef, lamb, pork, poultry, fish, dairy, eggs, fresh produce, nuts and grains, wine and finished products. We continue to expand our scope within beverages, seafood and other produce. We believe we offer the most comprehensive verification solutions in the industry.
10-k.txt:613: ● | To offer solutions for all participants in the food supply chain, including feed and input ingredient providers, farmers, producers, integrators, packers, auction barns, processors, handlers, distributors, restaurants, retailers and consumers.
10-k.txt:614: ● | To continue organic growth. We leverage our bundling capability to aggressively pursue new customers, while sustaining our recurring revenue model and high retention rates. We help new and existing customers create a program specific to their brand. As long as their process or claim can be standardized, we can create an audit platform to measure it accurately and authentically.
10-k.txt:615: ● | To continue growth through merger and acquisition opportunities. Through selective acquisitions, we can expand our footprint by adding new customers, services, food groups and revenue streams.
10-k.txt:616: INDUSTRY
10-k.txt:617: BACKGROUND
10-k.txt:618: The
10-k.txt:619: value-added food industry has been growing rapidly for the past several years in response to increased consumer interest about social
10-k.txt:620: responsibility, sustainability and food safety production practices. We continue to see a growing interest from consumers regarding how
10-k.txt:621: their food is produced. We are in an increasingly global food market with food products traveling around the world, and brands differentiating
10-k.txt:622: themselves in the market. These key drivers are increasing the number of food labeling claims made on food products.
10-k.txt:623: Natural
10-k.txt:624: and/or organic are examples of food labels that indicate that the food or other agricultural product has been produced in a certain way.
10-k.txt:625: Natural and organic sales are only part of the story of how consumers look for the verification of practices tied to food labeling claims.
10-k.txt:626: Other factors are also becoming increasingly more important to consumers, evidenced on menus and product labels. While not an exhaustive
10-k.txt:627: list, some of the issues that farms, ranches, producers, processors, restaurants and retailers are addressing include how animals are
10-k.txt:628: cared for and handled, how a product’s production impacts the environment and societies, and what inputs were used in the production
10-k.txt:629: of food items (like antibiotics).
10-k.txt:630: 4
10-k.txt:631: As
10-k.txt:632: consumers want more assurance about the trustworthiness of labeling claims, there is a growing trend for verification of practices around
10-k.txt:633: sustainability. As the agriculture, livestock and food industries continue to mature and expand internationally, there is an increasing
10-k.txt:634: need to record, manage, report and verify information regarding the source, age, genetic background, animal husbandry, environmental
10-k.txt:635: stewardship, practices surrounding the people and community, and other credence attributes. We believe verification of labeling claims
10-k.txt:636: by an independent third-party can meet consumer demands and expectations. Third-party verification also benefits producers, processors,
10-k.txt:637: distributors, restaurants, and retailers by addressing marketplace differentiation and global competitiveness.
10-k.txt:638: Current
10-k.txt:639: Marketplace Opportunities
10-k.txt:640: Because
10-k.txt:641: of growing demand for increased transparency into food production practices, we believe there are three main market drivers to promote
10-k.txt:642: forward momentum for our business:
10-k.txt:643: Market
10-k.txt:644: Driver #1 - Consumer awareness and expectations
10-k.txt:645: ● | Per Steve Stouffer, group president of Tyson Fresh Meats, “We recognize the importance of sustainable beef production practices that take care of people, the planet and animals. Our goal is to work with ranchers to verify (via a third-party) and, when possible, improve those practices so that we can be transparent with our customers and consumers about how cattle in our supply chain are raised.” The March 9, 2023 blog page titled “Creating a Pathway to a More Sustainable Beef Industry” written by Dr. Justin Ransom and Chad Martin continues to repeat this idea, “Through the Climate-Smart Beef Program, we (Tyson) can now track beef emissions at the individual animal level and work with our feedlot partners to share the data with producers so they can continue to build on their sustainable agriculture practices. To model these emissions, data – for example, farm management data and operational information – is collected and verified through third-party auditors such as Where Food Comes From, Inc. …At Tyson Foods, we believe the future of beef can be both climate-friendly and consumer-friendly.”
10-k.txt:646: ● | The JanahCyle.org September 11, 2024 blog page titled “Building Trust in Food and Beverage Brands through Purpose-Driven Marketing” states “…As consumer expectations continue to shift, food and beverage brands must adapt. Purpose-driven marketing isn’t just a trend - it’s a necessity. Brands that commit to transparency, sustainability, and ethical practices will be the ones that thrive… In the end, consumers want to trust that the brands they support are doing their part to make the world a better place. By staying true to their purpose, food and beverage brands can rebuild and maintain the trust that is essential to long-term success.

10-k.txt:1397: and certification revenues as it represents a value-added extension of our source verification. Verification and certification
10-k.txt:1398: service revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased approximately $0.5 million, or 2.2% compared to 2024. We continue to
10-k.txt:1399: experience new customer growth and bundling opportunities, but offsetting this growth are supply-side dynamics within the cattle
10-k.txt:1400: industry. The beef side of our business has been impacted the most significantly resulting in total verification revenues declining
10-k.txt:1401: about 6.5% in the fourth quarter of 2025 compared to 2024. We know the cattle industry is cyclical in nature and based on the data
10-k.txt:1402: from the USDA, we appear to be at the bottom of a contraction phase within the cattle cycle, however, we are still seeing signs of
10-k.txt:1403: further contraction in the cattle industry in early 2026. We are also facing rapidly changing trade and tariff uncertainties.
10-k.txt:1404: Because of the tight cattle supply, ranchers are receiving the highest cattle prices per head in a decade without verification; and
10-k.txt:1405: beef packers are reluctant to incur additional costs of verification to their supply chain because of the high costs of acquiring
10-k.txt:1406: cattle for slaughter. To expand supply, herds must be rebuilt within the United States and via imports. But rebuilding of the herd
10-k.txt:1407: takes time and is impacted by many factors including drought conditions in different regions, the price of inputs and interest
10-k.txt:1408: rates. We are encouraged because premiums for verified cattle remain strong in the marketplace above commodity cattle prices in spite of significant
10-k.txt:1409: pressure on beef packer margins. Verified product attributes like animal care, sustainability and natural continued to be demanded
10-k.txt:1410: and our programs allow supply chains to meet this growing customer demand. We are also optimistic about the recent launch of our Raisewell Certified Standard, which was developed to meet growing
10-k.txt:1411: consumer and retailer demand for responsibly raised proteins.

10-k.txt:1413: product sales are an ancillary part of our verification and certification services and represent sales of cattle identification ear tags.

10-k.txt:1416: overall beef cow inventories have declined from 28.9 million head on January 1, 2023 to 28.2 million head on January 1, 2024 and is now

exhibit-99-1.txt:32: CASTLE
exhibit-99-1.txt:33: ROCK, Colo., Nov. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Where Food Comes From, Inc. (WFCF) (Nasdaq: WFCF), the most trusted resource for
exhibit-99-1.txt:34: independent, third-party verification of food production practices in North America, today announced financial results for its third
exhibit-99-1.txt:35: quarter and nine-month period ended September 30, 2026.
exhibit-99-1.txt:36: “We
exhibit-99-1.txt:37: are pleased to report strong third quarter financial results highlighted by 6% growth in our core verification and certification business
exhibit-99-1.txt:38: that is benefitting from resurgent demand for beef-related services and growing momentum in other service offerings,” said John
exhibit-99-1.txt:39: Saunders, Chairman and CEO. “Our profit metrics also showed continued strength with gross margins rising by 380 basis points to
exhibit-99-1.txt:40: 42.1% and operating income growing 68% to $1.0 million from $600,000 a year ago – both reflecting the positive impact of our ongoing
exhibit-99-1.txt:41: cost down initiatives in conjunction with accelerating revenue.
exhibit-99-1.txt:42: “Our
exhibit-99-1.txt:43: ability to generate these results in the face of continued headwinds in our beef-related business underscores the importance of our diverse
exhibit-99-1.txt:44: and growing services portfolio. Although smaller cattle herd sizes have impacted product sales and certain verification services, newly
exhibit-99-1.txt:45: developed service offerings such as CARE and RaiseWell® Certified are growing rapidly and more than compensating. And, despite record
exhibit-99-1.txt:46: high beef prices, cattle producers are still capturing $100-per-head premiums when they use our value-add services. Additionally, we
exhibit-99-1.txt:47: are adding hundreds of new customers for our Organic, non-GMO, Gluten Free and Upcycled certifications, and we are benefitting from our
exhibit-99-1.txt:48: unique ability to offer service bundling that reduces costs and audit fatigue for our customers. With market research indicating that
exhibit-99-1.txt:49: consumer interest in sustainability, humane handling, and overall transparency in food raising practices has never been higher, our comprehensive
exhibit-99-1.txt:50: portfolio of services ideally positions us to continue leading our industry for years to come.”

# Course operating rules

These are harness rules. They are not part of a role's identity, values, or scoring criteria.

- Use only the evidence included in the JSON hand-off.
- Put an exact filing-line citation or an exact `facts.json` citation immediately after every filing number.
- Put an exact `calculations.json` citation immediately after every code-calculated number.
- Do not use a web number in the graded report.
- Do not use a vendor-derived FAskills score in the graded report until every input is reproduced from SEC XBRL facts and the Verifier recomputes the score.
- Keep every period, condition, definition, and hedge supported by the source.
- Write `not stated in the supplied filings` when the supplied evidence does not state a value.
- Never calculate inside a model role.
- Preserve GAAP and adjusted labels.
- Name the denominator definition for every margin and peer comparison.
- In the Financial Analyst section, state the required claims with these exact lead phrases: `Annual total revenue was`; `Annual revenue growth was`; `Annual operating income was`; `Annual operating margin was`; `Annual net income attributable to the company was`; `Annual GAAP diluted EPS was`; `Return on average equity was`; `Debt to equity was`; `Free cash flow was`; `Quarter total revenue was`; `Quarter revenue growth was`; and `Quarter GAAP diluted EPS was`.
- Put each required claim on its own line. Do not add a second number to a required-claim line.
- Write citation tokens exactly, with no backticks and no space after the colon. Valid examples are `(10-k.txt:1294)`, `(facts.json:total_revenue)`, `(calculations.json:revenue_growth)`, `(peers.json:WMT:operating_margin)`, and `(manifest.json:price)`.
- Use one citation token for one source. Do not combine two source names inside one pair of parentheses.
- Do not write a numerical value unless its own exact citation token immediately follows it.
- Do not put one citation at the end of a sentence to support several numbers. Put the matching citation immediately after each number.
- Use only a supplied `calculations.json` result for a numerical gap, difference, growth rate, ratio, or basis-point comparison. Never derive it inside a model role.
- Cite each peer operating margin as `(peers.json:TICKER:operating_margin)`.
- Cite the supplied share price as `(manifest.json:price)`.
- Give every numerical criterion score a same-line filing or calculation citation for the evidence used to assign that score.
- End each analyst output with one final nonblank line that begins exactly `Insight:`.
- The Insight must use exact supplied citation tokens and must not merely restate the earnings release's first paragraph.
- If an Insight uses a `calculations.json` result, include at least one reported input and its exact filing-line citation.
- A four-digit year may appear as a period label when the associated claim has an exact source citation. Do not remove a source-supported year from a period label.
- In `What would change my view`, state a direction or condition. Do not invent a numerical threshold unless the supplied evidence or a supplied code calculation states it.

Research Analyst.output:
# Overview

Where Food Comes From, Inc. (WFCF) operates as a third-party verification provider for food production practices in North America, supporting approximately 17,500 customers including farmers, ranchers, processors, and retailers (10-k.txt:553). The company’s primary business involves conducting on-site and desk audits to verify claims regarding livestock, aquaculture, crops, and other food products, supplemented by professional consulting services and a retail labeling program (10-k.txt:556). For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, total revenues were $24,892,000, a decrease from $25,746,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1369). This decline was driven by a 2.2% decrease in verification and certification service revenue to $20,102,000 and a 4.9% decrease in product sales to $3,616,000, primarily due to supply-side dynamics in the cattle industry and smaller beef cow herd sizes (10-k.txt:1398). Gross margin for 2025 decreased to 38.8% from 41.9% in 2024, attributed to inflationary price increases from cattle ear tag manufacturers and competitive market conditions (10-k.txt:1431). Segment operating income declined to $1,206,000 in 2025 from $2,207,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1387).

In the third quarter of 2026, the company reported a reversal in trend, with total revenue increasing 4% to $7,326,000 from $7,015,000 in the same quarter of 2025 (exhibit-99-1.txt:158). Verification and certification service revenue grew 6% to $5,897,000, while product sales remained flat at $1,211,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:155). Gross margin improved by 380 basis points to 42.1% from 38.3%, reflecting operational efficiencies and cost-down initiatives (exhibit-99-1.txt:59). Operating income increased 68% to $966,000 from $575,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:166). Management attributes this improvement to resurgent demand for beef-related services and growing momentum in new service offerings such as CARE and RaiseWell® Certified (exhibit-99-1.txt:37).

# Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

**Business-Model Durability: 3** The company’s business model relies on recurring verification audits and ancillary product sales. While the core verification service provides recurring revenue, the 2025 decline in total revenues to $24,892,000 and the 2.2% drop in verification revenue to $20,102,000 indicate vulnerability to cyclical agricultural trends (10-k.txt:1369). The 2026 Q3 recovery in verification revenue to $5,897,000 suggests some durability, but the reliance on cattle herd sizes for product sales (flat at $1,211,000 in Q3 2026) limits diversification (exhibit-99-1.txt:156).

**Customer Retention / Primary Operating KPI: 3** The company states it supports more than 17,500 customers (10-k.txt:553). Management notes "high retention rates" and "new customer growth" in 2025, but these were offset by supply-side dynamics in the cattle industry (10-k.txt:1399). In Q3 2026, management reported "adding hundreds of new customers for our Organic, non-GMO, Gluten Free and Upcycled certifications" (exhibit-99-1.txt:47). However, the flat product sales in Q3 2026 ($1,211,000 vs. $1,202,000) suggest that customer engagement in the beef sector remains constrained by herd size (exhibit-99-1.txt:156).

**Organic Growth: 3** The company cites a 19-year CAGR of approximately 17.87% from 2006 to 2025 (10-k.txt:609). However, 2025 total revenue declined to $24,892,000 from $25,746,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1369). In Q3 2026, organic growth in verification services was 6% to $5,897,000, driven by "resurgent demand for beef-related services" (exhibit-99-1.txt:155). The nine-month 2026 verification revenue of $15,710,000 represents a 4% increase over the prior year period (exhibit-99-1.txt:155).

**Expansion-Driven Growth: Not scored**
The filings mention growth through "merger and acquisition opportunities" (10-k.txt:615) and a past divestiture of Progressive Beef interest (exhibit-99-1.txt:69). However, no specific recent acquisitions or expansion-driven revenue figures are provided in the supplied 2025 10-K or Q3 2026 earnings release to score this criterion.

**Competitive Advantage: 4** The company positions itself as "one of the nation’s largest independent, third-party traceability and verification providers" (10-k.txt:577). It claims to offer "the most comprehensive verification solutions in the industry" by covering more food groups than any other provider (10-k.txt:612). The ability to bundle services to reduce "audit fatigue" for customers is cited as a unique advantage (exhibit-99-1.txt:48). The $100-per-head premium captured by cattle producers using WFCF services, even in a high-price environment, indicates strong value proposition (exhibit-99-1.txt:46).

**Catalyst Evidence: 4** Management highlights the "recent launch of our Raisewell Certified Standard" to meet growing demand for responsibly raised proteins (10-k.txt:1410). In Q3 2026, management noted that "newly developed service offerings such as CARE and RaiseWell® Certified are growing rapidly and more than compensating" for headwinds in the beef business (exhibit-99-1.txt:45). The improvement in gross margin to 42.1% in Q3 2026 from 38.3% in Q3 2025 is attributed to "ongoing cost down initiatives" (exhibit-99-1.txt:40).

**Moat Risk: 3** The primary risk is the cyclical nature of the cattle industry. The 10-K notes that "the beef side of our business has been impacted the most significantly" due to tight cattle supply and high cattle prices, which reduce packer willingness to pay for verification (10-k.txt:1400). The decline in beef cow inventories from 28.9 million head in 2023 to less than 28 million head in 2024 negatively impacts product sales (10-k.txt:1416). Additionally, "rapidly changing trade and tariff uncertainties" are cited as a risk (10-k.txt:1403).

# Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

The company’s strategic focus is on expanding its portfolio of auditing standards and leveraging bundling capabilities to pursue new customers (10-k.txt:614). The launch of the RaiseWell Certified Standard and CARE services represents a strategic pivot toward sustainability and animal welfare verification, which management believes will drive future growth (10-k.txt:1410). The improvement in operating income in Q3 2026 to $966,000, up 68% year-over-year, suggests that cost management initiatives are effective (exhibit-99-1.txt:166).

**What would change my view:**
A measurable operating result in the next filing that would strengthen my conclusion is a year-over-year increase in total verification and certification service revenue for the full year 2026 that exceeds the 4% growth seen in the nine-month period, specifically driven by non-beef categories. A direction of change that would weaken my conclusion is a continued decline in product sales revenue in Q4 2026, which would indicate that the cattle herd contraction is not offsetting by new service adoption.

Insight: The non-headline operating KPI of gross margin, which improved to 42.1% in Q3 2026 from 38.3% in Q3 2025 (exhibit-99-1.txt:59), has a strategic consequence of enabling the company to sustain its stock buyback program, as evidenced by the $268,000 in value returned to stockholders in Q3 2026 (exhibit-99-1.txt:18), despite the cyclical headwinds in the beef sector.

# Overview

Where Food Comes From, Inc. (WFCF) operates as a third-party verification provider for food production practices in North America, supporting approximately 17,500 customers including farmers, ranchers, processors, and retailers (10-k.txt:553). The company’s primary business involves conducting on-site and desk audits to verify claims regarding livestock, aquaculture, crops, and other food products, supplemented by professional consulting services and a retail labeling program (10-k.txt:556). For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, total revenues were $24,892,000, a decrease from $25,746,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1369). This decline was driven by a 2.2% decrease in verification and certification service revenue to $20,102,000 and a 4.9% decrease in product sales to $3,616,000, primarily due to supply-side dynamics in the cattle industry and smaller beef cow herd sizes (10-k.txt:1398). Gross margin for 2025 decreased to 38.8% from 41.9% in 2024, attributed to inflationary price increases from cattle ear tag manufacturers and competitive market conditions (10-k.txt:1431). Segment operating income declined to $1,206,000 in 2025 from $2,207,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1387).

In the third quarter of 2026, the company reported a reversal in trend, with total revenue increasing 4% to $7,326,000 from $7,015,000 in the same quarter of 2025 (exhibit-99-1.txt:158). Verification and certification service revenue grew 6% to $5,897,000, while product sales remained flat at $1,211,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:155). Gross margin improved by 380 basis points to 42.1% from 38.3%, reflecting operational efficiencies and cost-down initiatives (exhibit-99-1.txt:59). Operating income increased 68% to $966,000 from $575,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:166). Management attributes this improvement to resurgent demand for beef-related services and growing momentum in new service offerings such as CARE and RaiseWell® Certified (exhibit-99-1.txt:37).

# Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

**Business-Model Durability: 3** The company’s business model relies on recurring verification audits and ancillary product sales. While the core verification service provides recurring revenue, the 2025 decline in total revenues to $24,892,000 and the 2.2% drop in verification revenue to $20,102,000 indicate vulnerability to cyclical agricultural trends (10-k.txt:1369). The 2026 Q3 recovery in verification revenue to $5,897,000 suggests some durability, but the reliance on cattle herd sizes for product sales (flat at $1,211,000 in Q3 2026) limits diversification (exhibit-99-1.txt:156).

**Customer Retention / Primary Operating KPI: 3** The company states it supports more than 17,500 customers (10-k.txt:553). Management notes "high retention rates" and "new customer growth" in 2025, but these were offset by supply-side dynamics in the cattle industry (10-k.txt:1399). In Q3 2026, management reported "adding hundreds of new customers for our Organic, non-GMO, Gluten Free and Upcycled certifications" (exhibit-99-1.txt:47). However, the flat product sales in Q3 2026 ($1,211,000 vs. $1,202,000) suggest that customer engagement in the beef sector remains constrained by herd size (exhibit-99-1.txt:156).

**Organic Growth: 3** The company cites a 19-year CAGR of approximately 17.87% from 2006 to 2025 (10-k.txt:609). However, 2025 total revenue declined to $24,892,000 from $25,746,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1369). In Q3 2026, organic growth in verification services was 6% to $5,897,000, driven by "resurgent demand for beef-related services" (exhibit-99-1.txt:155). The nine-month 2026 verification revenue of $15,710,000 represents a 4% increase over the prior year period (exhibit-99-1.txt:155).

**Expansion-Driven Growth: Not scored**
The filings mention growth through "merger and acquisition opportunities" (10-k.txt:615) and a past divestiture of Progressive Beef interest (exhibit-99-1.txt:69). However, no specific recent acquisitions or expansion-driven revenue figures are provided in the supplied 2025 10-K or Q3 2026 earnings release to score this criterion.

**Competitive Advantage: 4** The company positions itself as "one of the nation’s largest independent, third-party traceability and verification providers" (10-k.txt:577). It claims to offer "the most comprehensive verification solutions in the industry" by covering more food groups than any other provider (10-k.txt:612). The ability to bundle services to reduce "audit fatigue" for customers is cited as a unique advantage (exhibit-99-1.txt:48). The $100-per-head premium captured by cattle producers using WFCF services, even in a high-price environment, indicates strong value proposition (exhibit-99-1.txt:46).

**Catalyst Evidence: 4** Management highlights the "recent launch of our Raisewell Certified Standard" to meet growing demand for responsibly raised proteins (10-k.txt:1410). In Q3 2026, management noted that "newly developed service offerings such as CARE and RaiseWell® Certified are growing rapidly and more than compensating" for headwinds in the beef business (exhibit-99-1.txt:45). The improvement in gross margin to 42.1% in Q3 2026 from 38.3% in Q3 2025 is attributed to "ongoing cost down initiatives" (exhibit-99-1.txt:40).

**Moat Risk: 3** The primary risk is the cyclical nature of the cattle industry. The 10-K notes that "the beef side of our business has been impacted the most significantly" due to tight cattle supply and high cattle prices, which reduce packer willingness to pay for verification (10-k.txt:1400). The decline in beef cow inventories from 28.9 million head in 2023 to less than 28 million head in 2024 negatively impacts product sales (10-k.txt:1416). Additionally, "rapidly changing trade and tariff uncertainties" are cited as a risk (10-k.txt:1403).

# Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

The company’s strategic focus is on expanding its portfolio of auditing standards and leveraging bundling capabilities to pursue new customers (10-k.txt:614). The launch of the RaiseWell Certified Standard and CARE services represents a strategic pivot toward sustainability and animal welfare verification, which management believes will drive future growth (10-k.txt:1410). The improvement in operating income in Q3 2026 to $966,000, up 68% year-over-year, suggests that cost management initiatives are effective (exhibit-99-1.txt:166).

**What would change my view:**
A measurable operating result in the next filing that would strengthen my conclusion is a year-over-year increase in total verification and certification service revenue for the full year 2026 that exceeds the 4% growth seen in the nine-month period, specifically driven by non-beef categories. A direction of change that would weaken my conclusion is a continued decline in product sales revenue in Q4 2026, which would indicate that the cattle herd contraction is not offsetting by new service adoption.

Insight: The non-headline operating KPI of gross margin, which improved to 42.1% in Q3 2026 from 38.3% in Q3 2025 (exhibit-99-1.txt:59), has a strategic consequence of enabling the company to sustain its stock buyback program, as evidenced by the $268,000 in value returned to stockholders in Q3 2026 (exhibit-99-1.txt:18), despite the cyclical headwinds in the beef sector.

# Overview

Where Food Comes From, Inc. (WFCF) operates as a third-party verification provider for food production practices in North America, supporting approximately 17,500 customers including farmers, ranchers, processors, and retailers (10-k.txt:553). The company’s primary business involves conducting on-site and desk audits to verify claims regarding livestock, aquaculture, crops, and other food products, supplemented by professional consulting services and a retail labeling program (10-k.txt:556). For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, total revenues were $24,892,000, a decrease from $25,746,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1369). This decline was driven by a 2.2% decrease in verification and certification service revenue to $20,102,000 and a 4.9% decrease in product sales to $3,616,000, primarily due to supply-side dynamics in the cattle industry and smaller beef cow herd sizes (10-k.txt:1398). Gross margin for 2025 decreased to 38.8% from 41.9% in 2024, attributed to inflationary price increases from cattle ear tag manufacturers and competitive market conditions (10-k.txt:1431). Segment operating income declined to $1,206,000 in 2025 from $2,207,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1387).

In the third quarter of 2026, the company reported a reversal in trend, with total revenue increasing 4% to $7,326,000 from $7,015,000 in the same quarter of 2025 (exhibit-99-1.txt:158). Verification and certification service revenue grew 6% to $5,897,000, while product sales remained flat at $1,211,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:155). Gross margin improved by 380 basis points to 42.1% from 38.3%, reflecting operational efficiencies and cost-down initiatives (exhibit-99-1.txt:59). Operating income increased 68% to $966,000 from $575,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:166). Management attributes this improvement to resurgent demand for beef-related services and growing momentum in new service offerings such as CARE and RaiseWell® Certified (exhibit-99-1.txt:37).

# Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

**Business-Model Durability: 3** The company’s business model relies on recurring verification audits and ancillary product sales. While the core verification service provides recurring revenue, the 2025 decline in total revenues to $24,892,000 and the 2.2% drop in verification revenue to $20,102,000 indicate vulnerability to cyclical agricultural trends (10-k.txt:1369). The 2026 Q3 recovery in verification revenue to $5,897,000 suggests some durability, but the reliance on cattle herd sizes for product sales (flat at $1,211,000 in Q3 2026) limits diversification (exhibit-99-1.txt:156).

**Customer Retention / Primary Operating KPI: 3** The company states it supports more than 17,500 customers (10-k.txt:553). Management notes "high retention rates" and "new customer growth" in 2025, but these were offset by supply-side dynamics in the cattle industry (10-k.txt:1399). In Q3 2026, management reported "adding hundreds of new customers for our Organic, non-GMO, Gluten Free and Upcycled certifications" (exhibit-99-1.txt:47). However, the flat product sales in Q3 2026 ($1,211,000 vs. $1,202,000) suggest that customer engagement in the beef sector remains constrained by herd size (exhibit-99-1.txt:156).

**Organic Growth: 3** The company cites a 19-year CAGR of approximately 17.87% from 2006 to 2025 (10-k.txt:609). However, 2025 total revenue declined to $24,892,000 from $25,746,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1369). In Q3 2026, organic growth in verification services was 6% to $5,897,000, driven by "resurgent demand for beef-related services" (exhibit-99-1.txt:155). The nine-month 2026 verification revenue of $15,710,000 represents a 4% increase over the prior year period (exhibit-99-1.txt:155).

**Expansion-Driven Growth: Not scored**
The filings mention growth through "merger and acquisition opportunities" (10-k.txt:615) and a past divestiture of Progressive Beef interest (exhibit-99-1.txt:69). However, no specific recent acquisitions or expansion-driven revenue figures are provided in the supplied 2025 10-K or Q3 2026 earnings release to score this criterion.

**Competitive Advantage: 4** The company positions itself as "one of the nation’s largest independent, third-party traceability and verification providers" (10-k.txt:577). It claims to offer "the most comprehensive verification solutions in the industry" by covering more food groups than any other provider (10-k.txt:612). The ability to bundle services to reduce "audit fatigue" for customers is cited as a unique advantage (exhibit-99-1.txt:48). The $100-per-head premium captured by cattle producers using WFCF services, even in a high-price environment, indicates strong value proposition (exhibit-99-1.txt:46).

**Catalyst Evidence: 4** Management highlights the "recent launch of our Raisewell Certified Standard" to meet growing demand for responsibly raised proteins (10-k.txt:1410). In Q3 2026, management noted that "newly developed service offerings such as CARE and RaiseWell® Certified are growing rapidly and more than compensating" for headwinds in the beef business (exhibit-99-1.txt:45). The improvement in gross margin to 42.1% in Q3 2026 from 38.3% in Q3 2025 is attributed to "ongoing cost down initiatives" (exhibit-99-1.txt:40).

**Moat Risk: 3** The primary risk is the cyclical nature of the cattle industry. The 10-K notes that "the beef side of our business has been impacted the most significantly" due to tight cattle supply and high cattle prices, which reduce packer willingness to pay for verification (10-k.txt:1400). The decline in beef cow inventories from 28.9 million head in 2023 to less than 28 million head in 2024 negatively impacts product sales (10-k.txt:1416). Additionally, "rapidly changing trade and tariff uncertainties" are cited as a risk (10-k.txt:1403).

# Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

The company’s strategic focus is on expanding its portfolio of auditing standards and leveraging bundling capabilities to pursue new customers (10-k.txt:614). The launch of the RaiseWell Certified Standard and CARE services represents a strategic pivot toward sustainability and animal welfare verification, which management believes will drive future growth (10-k.txt:1410). The improvement in operating income in Q3 2026 to $966,000, up 68% year-over-year, suggests that cost management initiatives are effective (exhibit-99-1.txt:166).

**What would change my view:**
A measurable operating result in the next filing that would strengthen my conclusion is a year-over-year increase in total verification and certification service revenue for the full year 2026 that exceeds the 4% growth seen in the nine-month period, specifically driven by non-beef categories. A direction of change that would weaken my conclusion is a continued decline in product sales revenue in Q4 2026, which would indicate that the cattle herd contraction is not offsetting by new service adoption.

Insight: The non-headline operating KPI of gross margin, which improved to 42.1% in Q3 2026 from 38.3% in Q3 2025 (exhibit-99-1.txt:59), has a strategic consequence of enabling the company to sustain its stock buyback program, as evidenced by the $268,000 in value returned to stockholders in Q3 2026 (exhibit-99-1.txt:18), despite the cyclical headwinds in the beef sector.

10-k.txt:1393: Revenue
10-k.txt:1394: Verification
10-k.txt:1395: and certification service revenues consist of fees charged for verification audits and other verification and certification related
10-k.txt:1396: services that the Company performs for customers. Fees earned from our WFCF labeling program are also included in our verification
10-k.txt:1397: and certification revenues as it represents a value-added extension of our source verification. Verification and certification
10-k.txt:1398: service revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased approximately $0.5 million, or 2.2% compared to 2024. We continue to
10-k.txt:1399: experience new customer growth and bundling opportunities, but offsetting this growth are supply-side dynamics within the cattle
10-k.txt:1400: industry. The beef side of our business has been impacted the most significantly resulting in total verification revenues declining
10-k.txt:1401: about 6.5% in the fourth quarter of 2025 compared to 2024. We know the cattle industry is cyclical in nature and based on the data
10-k.txt:1402: from the USDA, we appear to be at the bottom of a contraction phase within the cattle cycle, however, we are still seeing signs of
10-k.txt:1403: further contraction in the cattle industry in early 2026. We are also facing rapidly changing trade and tariff uncertainties.
10-k.txt:1404: Because of the tight cattle supply, ranchers are receiving the highest cattle prices per head in a decade without verification; and
10-k.txt:1405: beef packers are reluctant to incur additional costs of verification to their supply chain because of the high costs of acquiring
10-k.txt:1406: cattle for slaughter. To expand supply, herds must be rebuilt within the United States and via imports. But rebuilding of the herd
10-k.txt:1407: takes time and is impacted by many factors including drought conditions in different regions, the price of inputs and interest
10-k.txt:1408: rates. We are encouraged because premiums for verified cattle remain strong in the marketplace above commodity cattle prices in spite of significant
10-k.txt:1409: pressure on beef packer margins. Verified product attributes like animal care, sustainability and natural continued to be demanded
10-k.txt:1410: and our programs allow supply chains to meet this growing customer demand. We are also optimistic about the recent launch of our Raisewell Certified Standard, which was developed to meet growing
10-k.txt:1411: consumer and retailer demand for responsibly raised proteins.
10-k.txt:1412: Our
10-k.txt:1413: product sales are an ancillary part of our verification and certification services and represent sales of cattle identification ear tags.
10-k.txt:1414: Product sales for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased approximately $0.2 million or 4.9% compared to 2024. We continue to see
10-k.txt:1415: some new customer growth, but our customers are ordering less tags due to smaller beef cow herd size. According to the USDA statistics,
10-k.txt:1416: overall beef cow inventories have declined from 28.9 million head on January 1, 2023 to 28.2 million head on January 1, 2024 and is now
10-k.txt:1417: estimated at less than 28 million head. The tight cattle supply and weakened demand for verified cattle is negatively
10-k.txt:1418: impacting our product sales. Additionally, some customers received free tags under the USDA’s program
10-k.txt:1419: to jumpstart efforts to enable the fastest possible response to a foreign animal disease in connection with its definitive traceability
10-k.txt:1420: regulation, mandating the use of electronic ID tags for specific interstate movements of cattle and bison.

10-k.txt:1422: services revenue includes a wide range of professional consulting, data analysis, reporting and technology solutions that support our
10-k.txt:1423: verification business and generate incremental revenue specific to the food and agricultural industry. Our consulting revenue stream
10-k.txt:1424: is predominantly project based and not recurring in nature. For the year ended December 31, 2025, professional service revenue decreased
10-k.txt:1425: approximately $0.2 million over 2024.

exhibit-99-1.txt:32: CASTLE
exhibit-99-1.txt:33: ROCK, Colo., Nov. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Where Food Comes From, Inc. (WFCF) (Nasdaq: WFCF), the most trusted resource for
exhibit-99-1.txt:34: independent, third-party verification of food production practices in North America, today announced financial results for its third
exhibit-99-1.txt:35: quarter and nine-month period ended September 30, 2026.
exhibit-99-1.txt:36: “We
exhibit-99-1.txt:37: are pleased to report strong third quarter financial results highlighted by 6% growth in our core verification and certification business
exhibit-99-1.txt:38: that is benefitting from resurgent demand for beef-related services and growing momentum in other service offerings,” said John
exhibit-99-1.txt:39: Saunders, Chairman and CEO. “Our profit metrics also showed continued strength with gross margins rising by 380 basis points to
exhibit-99-1.txt:40: 42.1% and operating income growing 68% to $1.0 million from $600,000 a year ago – both reflecting the positive impact of our ongoing
exhibit-99-1.txt:41: cost down initiatives in conjunction with accelerating revenue.
exhibit-99-1.txt:42: “Our
exhibit-99-1.txt:43: ability to generate these results in the face of continued headwinds in our beef-related business underscores the importance of our diverse
exhibit-99-1.txt:44: and growing services portfolio. Although smaller cattle herd sizes have impacted product sales and certain verification services, newly
exhibit-99-1.txt:45: developed service offerings such as CARE and RaiseWell® Certified are growing rapidly and more than compensating. And, despite record
exhibit-99-1.txt:46: high beef prices, cattle producers are still capturing $100-per-head premiums when they use our value-add services. Additionally, we
exhibit-99-1.txt:47: are adding hundreds of new customers for our Organic, non-GMO, Gluten Free and Upcycled certifications, and we are benefitting from our
exhibit-99-1.txt:48: unique ability to offer service bundling that reduces costs and audit fatigue for our customers. With market research indicating that
exhibit-99-1.txt:49: consumer interest in sustainability, humane handling, and overall transparency in food raising practices has never been higher, our comprehensive
exhibit-99-1.txt:50: portfolio of services ideally positions us to continue leading our industry for years to come.”

exhibit-99-1.txt:111: About
exhibit-99-1.txt:112: Where Food Comes From, Inc.
exhibit-99-1.txt:113: Where Food Comes From, Inc. is America’s trusted resource for third party verification of
exhibit-99-1.txt:114: food production practices. Through proprietary technology and patented business processes, the Company estimates that it supports more
exhibit-99-1.txt:115: than 17,500 farmers, ranchers, vineyards, wineries, processors, retailers, distributors, trade associations, consumer brands and restaurants
exhibit-99-1.txt:116: with a wide variety of value-added services. Where Food Comes From solutions are used to verify food claims, optimize production practices
exhibit-99-1.txt:117: and enable food supply chains with analytics and data driven insights. In addition, the Company’s Where Food Comes From® retail
exhibit-99-1.txt:118: and restaurant labeling program uses web-based customer education tools to connect consumers to the sources of the food they purchase,
exhibit-99-1.txt:119: increasing meaningful consumer engagement for our clients.

# Overview

Where Food Comes From, Inc. (WFCF) operates as a third-party verification provider for food production practices in North America, supporting approximately 17,500 customers including farmers, ranchers, processors, and retailers (10-k.txt:553). The company’s primary business involves conducting on-site and desk audits to verify claims regarding livestock, aquaculture, crops, and other food products, supplemented by professional consulting services and a retail labeling program (10-k.txt:556). For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, total revenues were $24,892,000, a decrease from $25,746,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1369). This decline was driven by a 2.2% decrease in verification and certification service revenue to $20,102,000 (10-k.txt:1366) and a 4.9% decrease in product sales to $3,616,000 (10-k.txt:1367), primarily due to supply-side dynamics in the cattle industry and smaller beef cow herd sizes (10-k.txt:1398). Gross margin for 2025 decreased to 38.8% from 41.9% in 2024, attributed to inflationary price increases from cattle ear tag manufacturers and competitive market conditions (10-k.txt:1431). Segment operating income declined to $1,206,000 in 2025 from $2,207,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1387).

In the third quarter of 2026, the company reported a reversal in trend, with total revenue increasing 4% to $7,326,000 from $7,015,000 in the same quarter of 2025 (exhibit-99-1.txt:158). Verification and certification service revenue grew 6% to $5,897,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:155), while product sales remained flat at $1,211,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:156). Gross margin improved by 380 basis points to 42.1% from 38.3%, reflecting operational efficiencies and cost-down initiatives (exhibit-99-1.txt:59). Operating income increased 68% to $966,000 from $575,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:166). Management attributes this improvement to resurgent demand for beef-related services and growing momentum in new service offerings such as CARE and RaiseWell® Certified (exhibit-99-1.txt:37).

# Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

**Business-Model Durability: 3** The company’s business model relies on recurring verification audits and ancillary product sales. While the core verification service provides recurring revenue, the 2025 decline in total revenues to $24,892,000 (10-k.txt:1369) and the 2.2% drop in verification revenue to $20,102,000 (10-k.txt:1366) indicate vulnerability to cyclical agricultural trends. The 2026 Q3 recovery in verification revenue to $5,897,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:155) suggests some durability, but the reliance on cattle herd sizes for product sales (flat at $1,211,000 in Q3 2026) (exhibit-99-1.txt:156) limits diversification.

**Customer Retention / Primary Operating KPI: 3** The company states it supports more than 17,500 customers (10-k.txt:553). Management notes "high retention rates" and "new customer growth" in 2025, but these were offset by supply-side dynamics in the cattle industry (10-k.txt:1399). In Q3 2026, management reported "adding hundreds of new customers for our Organic, non-GMO, Gluten Free and Upcycled certifications" (exhibit-99-1.txt:47). However, the flat product sales in Q3 2026 ($1,211,000 vs. $1,202,000) (exhibit-99-1.txt:156) suggest that customer engagement in the beef sector remains constrained by herd size.

**Organic Growth: 3** The company cites a 19-year CAGR of approximately 17.87% from 2006 to 2025 (10-k.txt:609). However, 2025 total revenue declined to $24,892,000 from $25,746,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1369). In Q3 2026, organic growth in verification services was 6% to $5,897,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:155), driven by "resurgent demand for beef-related services" (exhibit-99-1.txt:37). The nine-month 2026 verification revenue of $15,710,000 represents a 4% increase over the prior year period (exhibit-99-1.txt:155).

**Expansion-Driven Growth: Not scored**
The filings mention growth through "merger and acquisition opportunities" (10-k.txt:615) and a past divestiture of Progressive Beef interest (exhibit-99-1.txt:69). However, no specific recent acquisitions or expansion-driven revenue figures are provided in the supplied 2025 10-K or Q3 2026 earnings release to score this criterion.

**Competitive Advantage: 4** The company positions itself as "one of the nation’s largest independent, third-party traceability and verification providers" (10-k.txt:577). It claims to offer "the most comprehensive verification solutions in the industry" by covering more food groups than any other provider (10-k.txt:612). The ability to bundle services to reduce "audit fatigue" for customers is cited as a unique advantage (exhibit-99-1.txt:48). The $100-per-head premium captured by cattle producers using WFCF services, even in a high-price environment, indicates strong value proposition (exhibit-99-1.txt:46).

**Catalyst Evidence: 4** Management highlights the "recent launch of our Raisewell Certified Standard" to meet growing demand for responsibly raised proteins (10-k.txt:1410). In Q3 2026, management noted that "newly developed service offerings such as CARE and RaiseWell® Certified are growing rapidly and more than compensating" for headwinds in the beef business (exhibit-99-1.txt:45). The improvement in gross margin to 42.1% in Q3 2026 from 38.3% in Q3 2025 (exhibit-99-1.txt:59) is attributed to "ongoing cost down initiatives" (exhibit-99-1.txt:40).

**Moat Risk: 3** The primary risk is the cyclical nature of the cattle industry. The 10-K notes that "the beef side of our business has been impacted the most significantly" due to tight cattle supply and high cattle prices, which reduce packer willingness to pay for verification (10-k.txt:1400). The decline in beef cow inventories from 28.9 million head in 2023 to less than 28 million head in 2024 negatively impacts product sales (10-k.txt:1416). Additionally, "rapidly changing trade and tariff uncertainties" are cited as a risk (10-k.txt:1403).

# Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

The company’s strategic focus is on expanding its portfolio of auditing standards and leveraging bundling capabilities to pursue new customers (10-k.txt:614). The launch of the RaiseWell Certified Standard and CARE services represents a strategic pivot toward sustainability and animal welfare verification, which management believes will drive future growth (10-k.txt:1410). The improvement in operating income in Q3 2026 to $966,000, up 68% year-over-year (exhibit-99-1.txt:166), suggests that cost management initiatives are effective.

**What would change my view:**
A measurable operating result in the next filing that would strengthen my conclusion is a year-over-year increase in total verification and certification service revenue for the full year 2026 that exceeds the 4% growth seen in the nine-month period (exhibit-99-1.txt:22), specifically driven by non-beef categories. A direction of change that would weaken my conclusion is a continued decline in product sales revenue in Q4 2026, which would indicate that the cattle herd contraction is not offsetting by new service adoption.

Insight: The non-headline operating KPI of gross margin, which improved to 42.1% in Q3 2026 from 38.3% in Q3 2025 (exhibit-99-1.txt:59), has a strategic consequence of enabling the company to sustain its stock buyback program, as evidenced by the $268,000 in value returned to stockholders in Q3 2026 (exhibit-99-1.txt:18), despite the cyclical headwinds in the beef sector.

# Overview

Where Food Comes From, Inc. (WFCF) operates as a third-party verification provider for food production practices in North America, supporting approximately 17,500 customers including farmers, ranchers, processors, and retailers (10-k.txt:553). The company’s primary business involves conducting on-site and desk audits to verify claims regarding livestock, aquaculture, crops, and other food products, supplemented by professional consulting services and a retail labeling program (10-k.txt:556). For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, total revenues were $24,892,000, a decrease from $25,746,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1369). This decline was driven by a 2.2% decrease in verification and certification service revenue to $20,102,000 (10-k.txt:1366) and a 4.9% decrease in product sales to $3,616,000 (10-k.txt:1367), primarily due to supply-side dynamics in the cattle industry and smaller beef cow herd sizes (10-k.txt:1398). Gross margin for 2025 decreased to 38.8% from 41.9% in 2024, attributed to inflationary price increases from cattle ear tag manufacturers and competitive market conditions (10-k.txt:1431). Segment operating income declined to $1,206,000 in 2025 from $2,207,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1387).

In the third quarter of 2026, the company reported a reversal in trend, with total revenue increasing 4% to $7,326,000 from $7,015,000 in the same quarter of 2025 (exhibit-99-1.txt:158). Verification and certification service revenue grew 6% to $5,897,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:155), while product sales remained flat at $1,211,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:156). Gross margin improved by 380 basis points to 42.1% from 38.3%, reflecting operational efficiencies and cost-down initiatives (exhibit-99-1.txt:59). Operating income increased 68% to $966,000 from $575,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:166). Management attributes this improvement to resurgent demand for beef-related services and growing momentum in new service offerings such as CARE and RaiseWell® Certified (exhibit-99-1.txt:37).

# Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

**Business-Model Durability: 3** The company’s business model relies on recurring verification audits and ancillary product sales. While the core verification service provides recurring revenue, the 2025 decline in total revenues to $24,892,000 (10-k.txt:1369) and the 2.2% drop in verification revenue to $20,102,000 (10-k.txt:1366) indicate vulnerability to cyclical agricultural trends. The 2026 Q3 recovery in verification revenue to $5,897,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:155) suggests some durability, but the reliance on cattle herd sizes for product sales (flat at $1,211,000 in Q3 2026) (exhibit-99-1.txt:156) limits diversification.

**Customer Retention / Primary Operating KPI: 3** The company states it supports more than 17,500 customers (10-k.txt:553). Management notes "high retention rates" and "new customer growth" in 2025, but these were offset by supply-side dynamics in the cattle industry (10-k.txt:1399). In Q3 2026, management reported "adding hundreds of new customers for our Organic, non-GMO, Gluten Free and Upcycled certifications" (exhibit-99-1.txt:47). However, the flat product sales in Q3 2026 ($1,211,000 vs. $1,202,000) (exhibit-99-1.txt:156) suggest that customer engagement in the beef sector remains constrained by herd size.

**Organic Growth: 3** The company cites a 19-year CAGR of approximately 17.87% from 2006 to 2025 (10-k.txt:609). However, 2025 total revenue declined to $24,892,000 from $25,746,000 in 2024 (10-k.txt:1369). In Q3 2026, organic growth in verification services was 6% to $5,897,000 (exhibit-99-1.txt:155), driven by "resurgent demand for beef-related services" (exhibit-99-1.txt:37). The nine-month 2026 verification revenue of $15,710,000 represents a 4% increase over the prior year period (exhibit-99-1.txt:155).

**Expansion-Driven Growth: Not scored**
The filings mention growth through "merger and acquisition opportunities" (10-k.txt:615) and a past divestiture of Progressive Beef interest (exhibit-99-1.txt:69). However, no specific recent acquisitions or expansion-driven revenue figures are provided in the supplied 2025 10-K or Q3 2026 earnings release to score this criterion.

**Competitive Advantage: 4** The company positions itself as "one of the nation’s largest independent, third-party traceability and verification providers" (10-k.txt:577). It claims to offer "the most comprehensive verification solutions in the industry" by covering more food groups than any other provider (10-k.txt:612). The ability to bundle services to reduce "audit fatigue" for customers is cited as a unique advantage (exhibit-99-1.txt:48). The $100-per-head premium captured by cattle producers using WFCF services, even in a high-price environment, indicates strong value proposition (exhibit-99-1.txt:46).

**Catalyst Evidence: 4** Management highlights the "recent launch of our Raisewell Certified Standard" to meet growing demand for responsibly raised proteins (10-k.txt:1410). In Q3 2026, management noted that "newly developed service offerings such as CARE and RaiseWell® Certified are growing rapidly and more than compensating" for headwinds in the beef business (exhibit-99-1.txt:45). The improvement in gross margin to 42.1% in Q3 2026 from 38.3% in Q3 2025 (exhibit-99-1.txt:59) is attributed to "ongoing cost down initiatives" (exhibit-99-1.txt:40).

**Moat Risk: 3** The primary risk is the cyclical nature of the cattle industry. The 10-K notes that "the beef side of our business has been impacted the most significantly" due to tight cattle supply and high cattle prices, which reduce packer willingness to pay for verification (10-k.txt:1400). The decline in beef cow inventories from 28.9 million head in 2023 to less than 28 million head in 2024 negatively impacts product sales (10-k.txt:1416). Additionally, "rapidly changing trade and tariff uncertainties" are cited as a risk (10-k.txt:1403).

# Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

The company’s strategic focus is on expanding its portfolio of auditing standards and leveraging bundling capabilities to pursue new customers (10-k.txt:614). The launch of the RaiseWell Certified Standard and CARE services represents a strategic pivot toward sustainability and animal welfare verification, which management believes will drive future growth (10-k.txt:1410). The improvement in operating income in Q3 2026 to $966,000, up 68% year-over-year (exhibit-99-1.txt:166), suggests that cost management initiatives are effective.

**What would change my view:**
A measurable operating result in the next filing that would strengthen my conclusion is a year-over-year increase in total verification and certification service revenue for the full year 2026 that exceeds the 4% growth seen in the nine-month period (exhibit-99-1.txt:22), specifically driven by non-beef categories. A direction of change that would weaken my conclusion is a continued decline in product sales revenue in Q4 2026, which would indicate that the cattle herd contraction is not offsetting by new service adoption.

Insight: The non-headline operating KPI of gross margin, which improved to 42.1% in Q3 2026 from 38.3% in Q3 2025 (exhibit-99-1.txt:59), has a strategic consequence of enabling the company to sustain its stock buyback program, as evidenced by the $268,000 in value returned to stockholders in Q3 2026 (exhibit-99-1.txt:18), despite the cyclical headwinds in the beef sector.
